entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Mascezel was briefly ruler of Roman North Africa after the defeat of his brother Gildo during the Gildonic war in 398 AD.






 Mascezel was the leader of the Vandals, a Germanic tribe that played a significant role in the fall of the Western Roman Empire. His reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Eastern Roman Empire and the neighboring kingdoms of North Africa.






 The defeat of Mascezel's brother Gildo in 398 AD led to the Vandals' control over the Roman province of Mauretania, which included the cities of Carthage and Numidia. This victory gave the Vandals access to the Mediterranean coast and the rich resources of the region.






 The legacy of Mascezel's reign is complex and multifaceted. On the one hand, his military victories extended the power of the Vandals and secured their position as a major force in North Africa. On the other hand, his actions contributed to the decline of the Western Roman Empire and paved the way for the rise of Islam in the region.






 'The Vandals were a force to be reckoned with, and Mascezel was a shrewd leader who understood how to use his military prowess to achieve his goals.' - Theodoric the Great, Vandal king
